primary_evidence.claim: The stated two-host network-filesystem layout violates the documented and released-implementation WAL shared-memory deployment requirement.
WAL permits one writer with concurrent snapshot readers; end marks and page lookup describe the supported deployment, not cross-host correctness.
Checkpoint default is 1000 pages unless configured otherwise; progress uses shared wal-index state and reader marks; readers can limit backfill/reset; PASSIVE may return OK with incomplete work.
FULL syncs WAL commits; NORMAL lacks the extra per-commit sync and can lose recent commits after power loss/system crash. This does not establish network-storage durability.
Recovery reconstructs the wal-index from retained WAL, uses exclusive WAL lock-range coordination, and may yield BUSY to concurrent access. Timing and mount behavior remain unverified.

WAL is persistent database state; last-close cleanup is conditional on exclusive-lock acquisition, successful checkpoint and PERSIST_WAL handling. The wal-index is transient, reconstructed after crash, and is not persistent WAL custody.

Pinned SQLite 3.51.3 contains the WAL-reset fix; the frozen documentation supplies affected/fixed versions, backports, race and telemetry caveats. Same version survives the name/deployment change, without making unsupported WAL safe.

DEFERRED default, IMMEDIATE writer contention, WAL EXCLUSIVE/IMMEDIATE equivalence, savepoints, statement completion and transaction-error handling are supported; a generic transaction-page COMMIT warning requires journal-mode qualification.

In ordinary supported WAL use, an open reader on another connection does not itself force the writer's COMMIT to wait or return BUSY. The released commit path skips the rollback-mode EXCLUSIVE database lock and appends WAL frames.
NORMAL still synchronizes a new/reused WAL header on the writer's frame-writing path when syncHeader is enabled; moving checkpoints off-thread cannot guarantee zero foreground sync.
32 KiB is an index-block size and a usual small wal-index size, not a total upper bound. Additional blocks are mapped as frames grow.

No-shm EXCLUSIVE mode requires the sole accessing process before first WAL access; read-only/immutable opening is not a simultaneous cross-host writer workaround. Custom VFS alternatives exist, but no mapped source establishes a two-host exemption.
A read-to-write upgrade can fail SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT even after the other writer has committed; releasing the stale transaction and starting a new one is required.

defects.claim: A writer COMMIT can fail BUSY because another connection has an open reader, retained as a WAL-mode rule; Output1 additionally says each such contention probe must surface BUSY.
defects.finding: The generic transaction-page warning is not an ordinary WAL COMMIT rule. Readers can block checkpoint/reset and stale read upgrades can fail; neither means an ordinary reader blocks a separate writer's WAL COMMIT. The unsupported network layout also provides no deterministic BUSY oracle.
defects.counterexample: counterexamples.json: reader_does_not_block_commit; installed SQLite 3.46.1 committed update while another connection remained in a read transaction seeing its old snapshot. Supplemental only; selected-release evidence is the 3.51.3 source trace in P9.
defects.consequence: Misstates retained locking behavior and, for Output1, would label valid WAL reader/writer concurrency a failed test. Requires correcting the retained claim before accepting the whole source-linked recommendation.
defects.incorrect_rejection: Output1's proposed must-BUSY oracle would falsely reject normal successful WAL COMMIT; the core two-host deployment rejection is correct.

defects.claim: With NORMAL checkpoint is the only barrier, so separate-thread checkpointing avoids main-thread sync.
defects.finding: The frozen WAL documentation contains this simplified wording, but released 3.51.3 code initializes syncHeader, clears it for SQLITE_IOCAP_SEQUENTIAL, and invokes sqlite3OsSync with nonzero checkpoint sync flags while writing the new/reused header on the foreground WAL-frame path. NORMAL omits the extra ordinary per-commit sync; it does not imply a strict no-foreground-sync guarantee.
defects.counterexample: Static selected-release path: NORMAL produces nonzero CKPT_SYNC_FLAGS; syncHeader enabled and iFrame==0 leads through pagerWalFrames to walFrames header sqlite3OsSync. No fsync tracing or latency measurement was performed.
defects.consequence: An affected latency/operational promise is falsely retained as equivalent. The materiality is the zero-sync foreground guarantee, not a reversal of the valid power-loss durability caveat.

defects.claim: The wal-index backing file is <=32 KiB.
defects.finding: The frozen documentation says it rarely exceeds 32 KiB; released code supports multiple 32 KiB index blocks. A total upper bound is false.
defects.counterexample: counterexamples.json: wal_index_size.shm_bytes=65536 after 4200 updates with autocheckpoint disabled on installed SQLite 3.46.1. Selected-release support is the block-allocation code, not this different-version execution.
defects.consequence: A localized size statement is wrong; no candidate decision or resource budget relies on this bound, so it is nonmaterial to the deployment disposition.

defects.claim: Prior reader gaps were provisioned on one host.
defects.finding: The mapped untrusted prior F3 conditions require reader gaps; its unresolved workload-tuning items and cross-cutting item 2 leave reader-gap provision open. Neither brief nor changes establishes that gaps were actually provisioned.
defects.task_evidence: prior_state: F3 Conditions/Dependencies/Unresolved and Cross-cutting unresolved item 2; changes.json unchanged does not establish provision.
defects.consequence: The dependency table promotes an assumed/unresolved condition to an established prior fact. R3 still withdraws the size/progress guarantee and carries tuning open, so this isolated binding error is nonmaterial to the disposition.

Output2.proposed_test_assessment: The explicit deployment gate is decisive. Coherence/checkpoint/recovery/custody tests remain proposed diagnostics, not proof that the unsupported mount is safe. Recovery overlap must be controlled; clean-close checks must account for PERSIST_WAL/actual successful checkpoint and shared-memory custody is distinct from persistent WAL. Output2 does not propose Output1's must-BUSY COMMIT oracle and does not explicitly repeat Output1's zero-foreground-sync promise.

independent_comparison: Both have a supported narrow deployment rejection and a material retained COMMIT/BUSY error. Output1 additionally makes an incorrect foreground-sync promise and a must-BUSY test oracle. Output2's explicit size upper bound and reader-gap prior-state row are localized errors. No economic ranking, preferred winner or target grade is assigned.

reviewer_execution.release_limit: These executions are supplemental local SQLite 3.46.1 evidence, not tests of SQLite 3.51.3 or the two-host target deployment. Selected-release defects are independently grounded in actual version-3.51.3 source text.

blinding_limits: Neutral paths were preserved, but final headings and sources.json arm/path fields exposed method labels. Those labels were visible and were not used as evidence or authority to read source-arm paths.
